title: compose.py dual-mode CLAUDE.md generation — comprehension test agent identifies the wake path under both modes

questions.question: Read tests/comprehension/8697_fixtures/skill_polling_CLAUDE.md. What is the skill agent's wake mechanism in this configuration, and what is the FIRST thing the agent should do at startup?
questions.expected: Wake mechanism is polling via `/loop`. At startup the agent should verify GitHub Issues access (gh CLI), then read the interval from `.squidsquad/config.md` and invoke `/loop [INTERVAL]m execute one Ralph Loop cycle` to schedule repeating cycles. Each cycle is mechanical pre-cycle → creative work → mechanical post-cycle (cycle_pre.py / cycle_post.py).

questions.question: Read tests/comprehension/8697_fixtures/skill_events_CLAUDE.md. What is the skill agent's wake mechanism in THIS configuration, and how does the agent receive work?
questions.expected: Wake mechanism is event-driven via the Monitor tool streaming `python references/scripts/event_poll.py <role> --wait 5 --target`. Each line of stdout is one JSON event. Events are hints, not commands — the source of truth is the forge (`tracker.py work_queue()`), which the agent reads after every event to determine canonical state. `event_poll.py` advances the cursor in `working-state.md` automatically (atomic `.tmp` + `mv`) on each event. The agent processes one event at a time. There is NO completion-API — task completion is reflected by the next forge transition (e.g., `tracker.py transition` to pending-test), not a separate POST. The agent does NOT invoke `/loop` and does NOT run cycle_pre.py/cycle_post.py.

questions.question: Compare tests/comprehension/8697_fixtures/pm_polling_CLAUDE.md against tests/comprehension/8697_fixtures/pm_events_CLAUDE.md. What sections differ between them, and what stays the same?
questions.expected: Differs: the polling file contains the `On Startup` /loop section, the `Ralph Loop` overview with cycle-based step markers, and the polling status-bar phase list. The events file replaces that with the `Event-Driven Workflow` section describing Monitor tool setup, event types (assigned-to, stop-requested, status-transition), the read→act→complete processing flow, and explicit `What You Do NOT Do` items (no /loop, no cycle_pre/cycle_post). Stays the same: PM's domain responsibilities (oversight, verification, routing), tracker protocol, sub-skills like task-pickup, checkin, verification, vault, prohibitions — everything that is wake-mode-agnostic.

questions.question: In events mode (per skill_events_CLAUDE.md), if an agent receives an assigned-to event for issue #42, what is the agent's processing flow?
questions.expected: Events are hints, not direct commands. The agent: (1) treats the event as a wake signal — `event_poll.py` has already advanced the cursor in working-state.md atomically; (2) forge-reads via `tracker.py work_queue()` to get the canonical role queue (the event payload may be stale by the time it's processed, so the forge is always the source of truth); (3) picks up the deterministic top item from the queue — transition it to `status:in-progress`, write the issue number to the Task field in working-state.md, begin the role-specific work. The agent processes one item at a time atomically; mid-task events are not acted on until the current task completes (Case D). Task completion is reflected by the next `tracker.py transition` (e.g., to pending-test), NOT by a completion-API POST — there is no `/events/<event_id>/complete` step.

questions.question: Read both qa_polling_CLAUDE.md and qa_events_CLAUDE.md. Does the QA agent's verification responsibility differ between the two modes? Why or why not?
questions.expected: The verification responsibility itself does not differ between modes — QA verifies pending-test items against acceptance criteria in both. What differs is only how QA *wakes up* to do that verification: in polling mode QA wakes via /loop ticks and pulls work from the queue at cycle start; in events mode QA wakes via Monitor events when the harness dispatches assigned-to. The actual verification sub-skill, test commands, file conventions, prohibitions, and discussion protocol are mode-agnostic and identical between the two composed outputs.

questions.question: Read dm_events_CLAUDE.md. If an operator flipped `event-driven: yes` in config.md for DM, and a feature reaches pending-ship status, how does DM learn about it?
questions.expected: DM learns via a `status-transition` event emitted on the harness event bus when the item flips to `status:pending-ship` with `role:dm`. The Monitor tool, streaming `event_poll.py dm --wait 5 --target`, delivers the JSON event line to the DM session. DM treats the event as a wake hint, then forge-reads via `tracker.py work_queue()` to get the canonical pending-ship queue (the event payload may be stale). DM picks up the top item, performs delivery (CHANGELOG, README, version bump per role responsibilities), and the next status transition (pending-ship → shipped) via `tracker.py transition` is what signals completion — there is no completion-API POST. Bare comments on the issue do NOT wake DM (or any agent) — only status/label changes generate events. DM's special case for in-flight PR merges is documented in comment-handling: at the END of a task (merge resolves), DM re-reads comments once before the next pickup. DM does NOT poll the tracker on a /loop schedule in this mode.
